Ingham County Circuit Court: Everything You Need to Know

When it comes to legal matters, having the right information can make a significant difference. If you are a resident of Ingham County or have a case that requires legal proceedings in this area, you may need to familiarize yourself with the Ingham County Circuit Court. History of Ingham County Circuit Court

The Ingham County Circuit Court was established in 1838 as one of the original circuit courts in Michigan. At that time, the court had jurisdiction over all civil and criminal cases within the county. Over time, the court's jurisdiction has been refined, and it now handles only certain types of cases. The court has undergone several changes over the years, including the construction of a new courthouse in 1903 and several renovations and expansions in the years since.

Jurisdiction of Ingham County Circuit Court

The Ingham County Circuit Court has jurisdiction over civil and criminal cases that arise within Ingham County. It is one of the largest circuit courts in Michigan, with eight judges assigned to hear cases. The court's jurisdiction includes cases involving general civil disputes, family law matters, criminal cases, and probate matters.

The Ingham County Circuit Court is made up of eight judges who are elected to six-year terms. Types of Cases Handled by Ingham County Circuit Court

The Ingham County Circuit Court handles a wide range of cases, including:

  • Criminal cases: These cases involve crimes that are punishable by imprisonment or fines.
  • Civil cases: These cases involve disputes between individuals or organizations, such as breach of contract or personal injury cases.
  • Family law cases: These cases involve matters such as divorce, child custody, and child support.
  • Probate cases: These cases involve matters related to the estate of a deceased person, including the distribution of assets and the appointment of a guardian for minor children.
